clue.text: It lends optimism mainly to exploited people

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: pawns are people used by others for their own ends
hope is a feeling of optimism

explanation.surface: Something gives a sense of hope to people who are being taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It lends' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is the whole definition: a shop that lends money against goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker's shop advances loans to customers who leave valuables as security.

clue.text: Comes together without last-minute trouble

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: things that fuse join or merge

indicators.note: last points at the closing letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Things fall into place without any bother at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last-minute' reads as one idea, a late rush, but it really means the last letter of minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss is a commotion or bother, the same kind of minor trouble or disturbance.

clue.text: It's not hard to get down at start of year

parts.note: down is soft feathery material, fluff

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Getting depressed at the beginning of January isn't difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get down' suggests feeling low; here down is the soft stuff on a chick or a pillow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fluffy is light and soft in texture, the opposite of firm or rigid.

clue.text: Garden tool's more streamlined

parts.note: the letter S taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden gadget has been given a sleeker design.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S looks like grammar but supplies its own letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a powered line trimmer used to cut grass and weeds at edges of a lawn.

clue.text: Speaker's choice unsettling Lucy with a "bravo"

indicators.note: unsettling something disturbs its order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A public speaker chooses to rattle Lucy by shouting a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: The speaker seems to be a person addressing a crowd; the definition means the stock of words someone picks from.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocabulary is the range of words a person uses, the selection from which any talker chooses.

clue.text: Some lychee served as final course

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A few lychees are brought out to end the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles lyCHEE SErved.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British meal the cheese board traditionally comes last, after the dessert.

clue.text: Victim unconcerned when they take man away

indicators.note: taking away a man means removing a word for a male person from the word before

parts.note: he is a male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a victim through indifference when a man is abducted.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is removed from THEY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is a person injured or killed in an accident or war, a sufferer of harm.

clue.text: By unknown means, upset docile character

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: in algebra an unknown quantity is x, y or z

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled by unexplained methods and a meek person.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man is a submissive person who always agrees with superiors, compliant and meek.

clue.text: Work hard in attempt to get prize

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Put real effort into your bid to win the award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work hard' reads as an instruction but is two separate pieces, and H for hard comes from pencil grading.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or other award given to a winner, the token of victory.

clue.text: Head boy ducks out of extra responsibility

indicators.note: ducking out of somewhere means leaving it, so a letter departs the word
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head boy at school dodges additional duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head boy' looks like a school prefect, but it means only the letter B, which leaves BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The onus is the burden or duty that falls on someone, an obligation.

clue.text: Intricate fast dance holds one spellbound

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so the reworked letters wrap round another piece
intricate means complicated, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complex, quick dance captivates a watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fascinated is to be held enthralled, so captivated that one cannot look away.

clue.text: Her cry moves the stony-hearted

indicators.note: moves means shifts about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her weeping touches even the hard-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The stony-hearted seem to be unfeeling people; literally they are fruits with a stone at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a fruit with a hard stone, or pit, in its middle.

clue.text: Wrongly pretend son is the one with the answers

indicators.note: wrongly suggests letters set out incorrectly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistaken fake son claims he knows everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A respondent replies, as in a survey or a court case where the respondent answers a petition.

clue.text: Protected me with ardour when agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shielded the speaker passionately in a moment of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured means fitted with protective plating, shielded against attack.

clue.text: Colt spoilt with mistreatment

indicators.note: mistreatment means rough handling, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A young horse is ruined by being badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt looks like a young horse, but here it is the gun maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colt is a revolver made by the Colt company, so an example of a handgun.

clue.text: It's not American to be quaintly attractive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of Europe, Asia and Africa rather than the Americas
second meaning: charmingly traditional and old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Charming quaintness is something non-American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old World is the eastern hemisphere known before Columbus; old-world charm is pleasingly traditional.

clue.text: Far from simple to speak without direction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
N for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Talking aimlessly is far from easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside: N sits within ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, the opposite of plain or unadorned.

clue.text: Performing with former partner is difficult

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Being on stage alongside your ex is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting task makes great demands on someone, so it is hard to do.

clue.text: Condition of student found in open countryside

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student's state is discovered out in the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: L plates mark a learner driver in Britain, hence L for student.
explanation.definitionFit: Health is a person's physical or mental condition, as in good or poor health.

clue.text: Get intimate with old doctor in narrow boat

indicators.note: in places the altered letters inside the word for the vessel

parts.note: a canoe is a narrow paddled boat

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters before are altered in order

explanation.surface: Cuddling up with an elderly physician in a narrowboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old doctor' reads as an aged medic; doctor is in fact a verb acting on old.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, being physically affectionate.

clue.text: Go ape out East for a climax

indicators.note: out suggests disordered or wrong, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Going wild in the Orient to reach a thrilling finale.
explanation.walkthrough: To go ape is slang for going wild with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the highest point or culmination of something, a peak moment.

clue.text: They head off with 24 hours to reach the peak

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: People set out on a day-long trek to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' looks like setting out on a journey but removes the first letter of They.
explanation.definitionFit: One's heyday is the period of greatest success or vigour, the high point of a career.

clue.text: Pester son and girl to go back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Nagging a son and daughter to return home.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl stands for any girl's name; Sarah is the one that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to annoy persistently, the same as badgering or bothering someone.

clue.text: Wave on the way to get heavy equipment

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it, which fixes the order of the two pieces

parts.note: a roller is a long, heavy breaking wave

explanation.surface: Someone waves as they travel, in order to fetch a big machine.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A road roller is a heavy vehicle with a drum used to flatten road surfaces, an item of plant.

clue.text: Echoes note to singer

indicators.note: an echo throws a sound back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer's note reverberates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word but supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice, between soprano and tenor.

clue.text: Encourage to be offbeat

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so these letters are out of order

parts.note: the second half of this word is taken as written; the first half is the signal to rearrange it

explanation.surface: Urging someone to be quirky and unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offbeat' looks like a single word meaning quirky; split it into off and beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or assist someone, typically in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Man meets another returning home for dog

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: One man runs into another coming home to fetch the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel is a small shelter where a dog sleeps, its house.

clue.text: Eats vegetables — sounds like they are past their best

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to go by what is heard, not how it is written

parts.note: to have food is to eat it, and beans are vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone who eats greens is said to be over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a meal is to eat it, so eats becomes has.
explanation.definitionFit: Has-beens are people whose fame or success is behind them, faded figures.
